sections.h2: What does selling a house in De Pere, WI involve?
sections.html:
De Pere is a city in Brown County, about five miles south of Green Bay on the Fox River, with a 2025 Census Bureau estimate of 25,590 residents. A sale here runs through three local offices: the City of De Pere for permits and assessment, the Brown County Register of Deeds for the deed, and the Brown County Treasurer for tax records.

You can list with an agent, sell on your own, or accept a cash offer from a buyer who takes the house as it stands. The sections below cover the De Pere details that affect price and timing under each route.

sections.h2: What is De Pere like, and how does the layout affect a home sale?
sections.html:
De Pere grew up around the first and last rapids on the lower Fox River. A French Jesuit mission was founded there in 1671, and the city traces its modern plat to 1836, when the De Pere Hydraulic Company laid out the town. The east and west banks were separate municipalities for decades. East De Pere became a city in 1883, and West De Pere (briefly named Nicolet) was folded into it in 1890, according to the city's Wikipedia entry.

That two-bank history still shapes the market. Large older homes line Broadway, Ridgeway Boulevard, Morris, Fulton, Franklin and nearby streets close to the river, and several of those blocks sit in National Register historic districts. St. Norbert College, founded in 1898, borders the river on the west side. Newer subdivisions sit away from the water, with Interstate 41 running along the west side of the city and Highways 32 and 57 entering from the south.

The city says two school districts serve De Pere, so check which one covers your address before you tell a buyer. Wikipedia also notes that the Lower Fox River below the De Pere dam went through a cleanup of PCB-contaminated sediment that was completed in 2020. If you are selling a riverfront house, buyers are likely to ask about it, so it helps to have the answer ready.

sections.h2: How does De Pere assess property, and what can you do about it?
sections.html:
Since 2018 De Pere has reassessed every property each year, so the city's values stay close to market. The city contracts the work to Accurate Appraisal, LLC of Menasha, and its assessment page explains that an assessor does not set tax rates and that a revaluation does not raise the total tax the city collects. The city's own explainer reported an overall average increase of about 8 to 10 percent in the 2024 update.

  • Open Book is a short conference, in person or by phone, with an assessor to review your value.
  • If you still disagree, you can appeal to the Board of Review, a five-member board of residents appointed by the mayor.
  • You schedule that appearance through the City Clerk at 339-4050 and file a Formal Objection Application. State law treats the assessor's value as correct until you prove otherwise with facts.

The city tells owners to call the Brown County Treasurer at (920) 448-4074 when the mailing address for a property changes, so tax bills reach the right person. After a sale, give the treasurer the buyer's mailing address so the next bill goes to the right place, and ask the title company how the current year's tax is split at closing.

sections.h2: Which De Pere permit rules matter before you sell?
sections.html:
The city's Building Inspection page tells buyers they can request city building records to see whether permits were obtained and whether work passed inspection. That makes permit history a negotiation point. Before listing, ask the Building Department (920-339-4053, dpbldg@deperewi.gov) for the record on your parcel.

  • A permit is required for new construction, repairs, additions, alterations and demolitions, including boilers, furnaces, wiring, plumbing fixtures, garages, porches, fences, decks, swimming pools and sheds.
  • Starting work without a permit doubles the permit fee, and a stop work order can follow.
  • A building permit lasts one year, or two years for a one- or two-family dwelling.
  • Replacing windows or changing exits and light openings can also need a permit.

The city warns that projects not completed to code can affect a home's insurability and potential sale. If you find open work, finishing and closing the permit before you list often settles the question for a buyer. If you cannot meet zoning or code requirements, the Zoning Board of Appeals hears variance requests for a $175 fee.

sections.h2: Can you rent out a De Pere house before selling it?
sections.html:
Long-term tenants are common in De Pere, and the city also regulates short-term rentals. Anyone who rents a house on a platform like Airbnb or VRBO needs a Tourist Rooming House license, which in De Pere is a two-step process. You first apply to the Development Services Department with a $100 fee, and after approval the Health Department's sanitarian explains how to get the license. The city says you may not rent the property until the sanitarian completes a pre-inspection.

If your house has been used as a short-term rental, ask the city's Development Services Department about its license status before you list. A buyer who plans to continue the use will ask.

sections.h2: How do you record the deed at the Brown County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
De Pere deeds are recorded at the Brown County Register of Deeds, Northern Building Room 260, 305 E. Walnut Street, Green Bay. The office is open Monday to Thursday 7:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. and Friday 7:30 to 11:30 a.m., and walk-in real estate recordings are accepted until 4:30 p.m. Monday through Thursday and until 10:30 a.m. on Friday. The phone number is 920-448-4470.

Brown County has moved to tag-less recording. If you submit paper documents, you also submit a Swift Agreement, and you receive an email with a secure link that allows up to three printed copies for seven days.

The deed also needs the state transfer return. Wis. Stat. 77.22 sets the fee at 30 cents per $100 of value, paid by the grantor, and requires the return to be filed electronically. The register writes the fee on the face of the deed, and if a sale is exempt, the exemption reason must be stated on the deed.

sections.h2: What must a De Pere seller disclose to the buyer?
sections.html:
Chapter 709 applies to sales, exchanges and land contracts of property with one to four dwelling units, and to vacant land. The chapter's definition excludes dwellings that have never been inhabited. The owner completes the state's condition report and delivers it within 10 days after the contract is accepted.

If the report is late, the buyer has a short window to cancel. Personal representatives, trustees and conservators who never occupied the home are excused, which helps heirs selling an estate house in De Pere. Everyone else should answer every item, because a partly filled report is treated as incomplete.

sections.h2: Should you list, or sell your De Pere house for cash?
sections.html:
A listing suits a house that shows well and a seller who can wait on a buyer's financing. A cash sale suits a house with open permits, deferred maintenance, tenants, or a family estate to close.

Whatever the route, ask for a net sheet. It should show the loan payoff, the 30 cents per $100 transfer fee, recording, prorated taxes and any repair credit, so you compare actual proceeds and not asking prices.

faqs.q: Who assesses property in De Pere?
faqs.a: Accurate Appraisal, LLC of Menasha, under contract with the city. De Pere has assessed every property annually since 2018, and owners can attend an Open Book session to discuss a value.

faqs.q: Where is a De Pere deed recorded?
faqs.a: At the Brown County Register of Deeds in Green Bay. The office phone is 920-448-4470, and paper submissions need a Swift Agreement under the county's tag-less system.

faqs.q: What is the Wisconsin transfer fee on a De Pere sale?
faqs.a: It is 30 cents for each $100 of value, paid by the seller. On a $280,000 sale that is $840.

faqs.q: Can I rent my De Pere house on Airbnb before I sell?
faqs.a: Only with a Tourist Rooming House license. The city requires a $100 application to Development Services and a pre-inspection by the Health Department sanitarian before any rental.

faqs.q: Does unpermitted work stop a De Pere sale?
faqs.a: Buyers can request the city's building records, and open work can come up in negotiation. Starting work without a permit doubles the permit fee, so closing out permits before listing is usually cheaper.
